title: Fix race in burst fractionation + grace-period handling causing Dedicated pool shortfalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalations reported increased 95th/99th token latency and sporadic tail-rate 503s for tenants on Dedicated reserved pools during regional surges. Root cause traced to a race between the burst-credit fractionation routine (per-shard split to satisfy multi-tenant headroom) and the allocator grace-period timer. The race causes transient fragmentation of tenant burst credits across allocator shards, followed by premature eviction from warm slots when the grace window expires. Net effect: tenants hit cold-start latency and observed request drops during short bursts despite global pool capacity being available.
root_cause: The autoscaler/allocator performs a fractional split of pending burst credits across N allocator shards to allow fine-grained warm slot allocation. A grace-period timer was implemented to avoid holding warm slots indefinitely when partial credit wasn't consumed. Under high churn the split and the grace-period decrement run concurrently without synchronization. When a split task updates per-shard ledgers while the grace timer reads/writes the same ledger, some shards end up with zeroed credits and the tenant's warm-slot reference count drops to 0. The global fallback path exists but is rate-limited and subject to circuit backpressure, so observed requests were rerouted to cold pools or dropped during the convergence window.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: rolled out runtime feature-flag 'burst_fractionation_v2_disable' to force single-shard accounting for affected regions and disabled the grace timer decrement path for fractionated entries. 2) Emergency patch (PR #2345) added a per-tenant allocation lock and serialized ledger mutate operations to prevent mid-update zeroing. 3) Applied a temporary increase to global fallback rate limits for VIP customers to reduce 503s. 4) Notified impacted customers (ACME Health, NovaRetail) and enabled dedicated warm-prewarm policies for their tenants to absorb upcoming load.
timeline: 2026-03-02 03:41 UTC: Pager triggered — multiple Dedicated tenants reporting tail latency and 503s during a region surge. On-call ops triaged and linked telemetry (console dashboard incident 2026-03-02-77).
2026-03-02 04:05 UTC: Initial mitigation — increased fallback allowance for top customers and disabled aggressive eviction heuristics via runtime toggle.
2026-03-02 05:10 UTC: Engineering lead (Marco) reproduces scenario in staging with load replay; identifies ledger delta race between fractionation and grace-timer threads.
2026-03-02 09:20 UTC: Hotfix branch created; quick patch to serialize ledger writes + feature-flag rollout to EU-west and US-east. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
2026-03-02 12:30 UTC: Hotfix validation — no further 503s for replayed load; tail latency recovered to baseline for repro tenants.
2026-03-03 08:00 UTC: Customer comms — sent incident summary and temporary workarounds to ACME Health & NovaRetail. Support asked for temporary safety buffers in their reserved pools.
2026-03-05 10:45 UTC: Canary rollout of serialized ledger patch to all Dedicated regions behind feature flag.
2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: Code review completed for resilient fractionation v2; in-progress implementation includes stronger invariants and integrated tests.
notes: Decision: avoid optimistic fractionation until v2 implements atomic ledger swaps or shard-cohort consensus.
Trade-off: single-shard accounting increases contention at high QPS but guarantees no fragmentation-induced eviction; acceptable as an emergency fallback.
Follow-up: add inter-shard invariants and end-to-end chaos tests to the allocator simulation harness.
Operational: add an SLO alert on 'allocated_burst_credit_delta_per_tenant' and a synthetic test that exercises fractionation paths every 6 hours.
comm_cs_notes: Customer success updated ACME Health with timeline and mitigation; NovaRetail requested longer-term quota guarantees — scheduled for follow-up in account review meeting.
next_steps: 1) Merge fractionation-v2 with atomic swap semantics (ENG-135792). 2) Add allocator-level coarse-grained lock with metrics for contention (ENG-135793). 3) Release runtime-1.22 patch with backported fix to Dedicated tenants on 2026-03-19. 4) Implement synthetic end-to-end tests in chaos-suite and expand Canary window for 48h.
